speaker: Doctor
text: I understand you are here for bizarre and agitated behavior; to start, have you noticed any physical symptoms like fever, stiff muscles, or changes in your speech?

speaker: Patient
text: 26-year-old male. The patient has been demonstrating bizarre and agitated behavior for the past 6 weeks. He believes that he is being spied on by the NSA which is also controlling his mind. His wife adds that he has been increasingly withdrawn and intermittently depressed over the last 3 months. He was terminated from his job 4 weeks ago after he ceased attending work. Since his unemployment, he has been focused on creating a device to prevent people from controlling his mind.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Has he been experiencing hallucinations, such as hearing voices or seeing things that others do not? Additionally, have there been any significant changes in his sleep patterns or appetite?

speaker: Patient

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Delusional Disorder, Persecutory Type.

Based on the six-week duration of fixed, non-bizarre delusions regarding persecution (NSA control) without prominent hallucinations or mood symptoms dominating the clinical picture, this presentation aligns with Delusional Disorder rather than Schizophrenia or a primary mood disorder.
